body.objective: Students will be able to name school subjects.
successCriteria: I can name school subjects in Mandarin
I can say which subjects I like and dislike
I can ask a classmate about their favourite subject
body.hook: What's your favourite class? In China, students study many of the same subjects you do: Chinese, math, science, English and PE. Learning to talk about your school subjects lets you compare your school day with a student in Beijing or Shanghai.

study.title: 你最喜欢什么课？
study.question: How do I talk about school subjects in Mandarin?
study.passage:
More subjects: 历史 lìshǐ (history), 音乐 yīnyuè (music), 美术 měishù (art), 法文 Fǎwén (French).
Sentence patterns:
• 我喜欢数学。Wǒ xǐhuan shùxué. = I like math.
• 我不喜欢历史。Wǒ bù xǐhuan lìshǐ. = I don't like history.
• 你最喜欢什么课？Nǐ zuì xǐhuan shénme kè? = What is your favourite class?
• 我最喜欢体育课。Wǒ zuì xǐhuan tǐyù kè. = My favourite is PE class.
• 为什么？Wèishénme? = Why? 因为… yīnwèi… = Because…
Dialogue:
小明 Xiǎo Míng：你最喜欢什么课？
安娜 Ānnà：我最喜欢美术课。你呢？
小明：我最喜欢数学课。
安娜：为什么？
小明：因为数学很有意思。
安娜：我不喜欢数学，太难了！
English support: 你呢？nǐ ne? = And you? 很有意思 hěn yǒu yìsi = very interesting. 太难了 tài nán le = too hard!
Activity: Ask five classmates "你最喜欢什么课？" and record answers in a tally chart. Report: "三个同学最喜欢体育课。" (Sān gè tóngxué zuì xǐhuan tǐyù kè = Three classmates like PE class most.)
study.source: Original dialogue written for this lesson.
steps: Practise the 喜欢 and 不喜欢 patterns
Read the dialogue with a partner
discussion: What is Xiǎo Míng's favourite class, and why?
How do you make 喜欢 negative?
What does 你呢 mean, and when do you use it?
study.product: Write five sentences in characters and pinyin about your school subjects: two you like, one you don't, your favourite with a reason (因为), and one question for a classmate.

body.objective: Students will be able to tell time.
successCriteria: I can ask and tell the time in Mandarin
I can use 点, 分, 半, 刻 and 差
I can say when something happens
body.hook: 现在几点? Xiànzài jǐ diǎn? "What time is it now?" Telling time in Mandarin uses numbers you already know plus a few short words: 点 for o'clock, 分 for minutes, 半 for half.

vocabulary.term: 上午 / 下午 shàngwǔ / xiàwǔ

study.title: 现在几点?
study.question: How do I tell time in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Time guide (written for this lesson):
1:00 一点 yī diǎn. 2:00 两点 liǎng diǎn (use 两, not 二). 3:10 三点十分 sān diǎn shí fēn. 8:05 八点零五分 bā diǎn líng wǔ fēn.
4:30 四点半 sì diǎn bàn. 4:15 四点一刻 sì diǎn yí kè (or 四点十五分). 4:45 四点三刻 sì diǎn sān kè, or 差一刻五点 chà yí kè wǔ diǎn (a quarter to five).
Time of day comes first: 早上 zǎoshang (early morning), 上午 (morning), 中午 zhōngwǔ (noon), 下午 (afternoon), 晚上 wǎnshang (evening). 下午三点 = 3 p.m.
When: time goes before the verb: 我七点起床。Wǒ qī diǎn qǐchuáng. (I get up at 7.) 我们八点半上课。
Question: 现在几点? 你几点上学?
Activity: paper clocks with a partner; then ask each other 你几点起床? 你几点吃午饭?
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.
steps: Learn 半, 刻 and 差
Ask partners about their daily times
discussion: Why is 2:00 两点 and not 二点?
Where does the time go in a sentence?
When does your partner get up?

body.objective: Students will be able to describe my school day.
body.iCan: I can describe my school day.
successCriteria: I can describe my school day in Mandarin
I can use 上课, 下课, 放学 and time expressions

body.hook: Many schools in China start early, have a long lunch break, and include eye exercises and morning exercises for the whole school. How does your school day compare?

study.title: 我的一天
study.question: How do I describe my school day in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Text (read aloud, written for this lesson):
我每天早上七点起床。七点半吃早饭。八点半上课。我第一节课是数学。十二点吃午饭。下午三点放学。放学以后, 我先做作业, 然后打篮球。晚上十点睡觉。
Pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng. Qī diǎn bàn chī zǎofàn. Bā diǎn bàn shàngkè. Wǒ dì-yī jié kè shì shùxué. Shí'èr diǎn chī wǔfàn. Xiàwǔ sān diǎn fàngxué. Fàngxué yǐhòu, wǒ xiān zuò zuòyè, ránhòu dǎ lánqiú. Wǎnshang shí diǎn shuìjiào.
Grammar: 第 dì + number = ordinal: 第一节课 (first class). 以后 yǐhòu = after. 先…然后… = first… then….
School in China (general patterns): many schools start around 7:30–8:00, include morning exercises (课间操) and eye exercises (眼保健操), have a long lunch break where some students rest, and end later for older students who often have evening study. Students often stay in one classroom while teachers move.
Activity: write your school day in a timeline, then compare it with a Chinese school day in a T-chart.
study.source: Original text written for this lesson; school patterns are general and vary by region and school.
steps: Use 第, 以后 and 先…然后…
